overall: The AG found the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by not taking all votes by roll call during a remote-participation meeting and by missing the 14-business-day deadline to respond to a complaint. The notice-posting allegation was rejected, and no intentional violation or civil fine was found.

allegations.summary: Amended notice for the April 6 meeting allegedly omitted the date and time the original notice was posted.
allegations.key_passage: Because the April 2 notice was posted more than 48 hours before the April 6 meeting, and because it included the date and time it was posted, there was no violation of the Open Meeting Law in this instance.

allegations.summary: During the April 6 meeting with remote members, the Committee allegedly failed to take all votes by roll call; the Committee argued the Executive Order suspended remote participation rules.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, because the Committee failed to conduct roll call votes during the April 6 meeting, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant asked for a $1000 civil fine for the roll call failure as a willful violation.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Committee did not intentionally violate the law when it failed to take all votes by roll call at its April 6 meeting

allegations.summary: The Committee allegedly did not review or respond to the April 7 complaint until May 11, beyond the 14-business-day deadline.
allegations.key_passage: We find the Committee violated the Law where, without being granted an extension of time, it did not review or respond to the Complainant’s April 7 complaint until May 11, 23 business days after April 7.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint: the AG noted the April 6 notice did not clearly explain how the public could access the remote meeting. This was a recommendation only.
allegations.key_passage: Although the Committee attempted to inform the public how it could access the April 6 meeting, we recommend that the Committee include this information under the “Location of Meeting” section of its meeting notices going forward

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
